scope_notes: CullDegenerateMeshFaces accepts no arguments, reuses the Mesh confirmation getter, and stages every native result before one transaction. Surviving object IDs/attributes/groups/selection remain attached. Meshes losing all faces are deleted. Undo/Redo restores replacements/deletions together. No-ops and staging/stale-source failures preserve history and Redo. UI tests cover preselection, clicked postselection, Mesh filtering, cancellation, and the SelBadObjects-to-cleanup workflow.

A private-copy OpenNURBS DeleteComponents call uses the same degenerate-face executive as CullDegenerateFaces, with unused-vertex and empty-n-gon cleanup enabled. The explicit policy removes all unused vertex occurrences, including preexisting ones. Original-to-new face maps distinguish quad repairs from face removals; repairs can remove no face. Double coordinates and surviving color occurrences are retained without welding. Native classification is independent of document tolerance, including a 1e-36 cross-product-length floor and 1e-8 relative quad-diagonal criterion.

Only repair admission defers geometric validity and permits invalid raw face indices and finite native-unset coordinates. Pointer/count/span/finite/ownership and n-gon membership bounds remain checked; ordinary operations retain their validity gate. Native tests exercise repeated/out-of-range/UINT_MAX raw indices, fully empty results, no-op cleanup, mixed repairs/removals/orphans, colors, and small/remote/unwelded coordinates. The Rust document mesh API still requires distinct in-range stored indices.

Native deletion can leave a stale n-gon boundary when a repaired quad corner is still used elsewhere. The adapter refreshes invalid overlays with the shared native boundary routine. Existing Rust n-gon retention rebuilds or drops groups that no longer meet its topology rules. Tests retain the corrected single-face boundary, dissolve a disconnected group without welding facets, and preserve an unaffected annular hole through visible edges and MeshToNurb. This does not claim universal n-gon retention or SDK raw-overlay parity.

Thirteen actual-command oracle recipes use independent count/area expectations: valid triangles/quads, collinear/coincident triangles, collapsed/opposite-coincident/partial-zero-area quads, mixed bad faces, preexisting orphan vertices, unwelded duplicate panels, sub-float features at remote origins, and tiny faces on both sides of the native cutoff. CLI observations are freshly generated local results, not comparative timing evidence.

The public SDK profile copies an owned double-precision stored mesh, calls Faces.CullDegenerateFaces and then Vertices.CullUnused, and observes raw double-coordinate records plus before/after counts and area. It does not infer quad repairs from the removal return value, normalize n-gons, or emulate Rhino document deletion/getters. Empty output reports empty geometry, not document parity. SDK mocks cover copy/null/alias and native/mass/observation failures, disposal, zero-return repairs, no-op/empty/orphan post-counts, strict input, actual worker routing, and isolated host staging of transitive helper modules.

AddressSanitizer instruments the shared OpenNURBS modeling archive and C ABI. Eleven bridge tests and five geometry cleanup tests pass; leak detection and optional stack-use-after-return detection are disabled. Bundled allocator/font/compression dependencies are not separately instrumented. This is targeted evidence, not a general memory-safety certificate.

No fresh licensed Rhino capture was attempted in this increment. The latest recorded launch problem remains docs/oracle-sspi.md. Full command/getter parity and comparative performance remain unqualified. usd-brep is unchanged; this operation is polygon mesh cleanup using the existing shared OpenNURBS archive.

Fifteen historical source hashes in four verifiable qualification records are retained through immutable Git references. Their non-hash fields are unchanged; 69 pre-existing unverifiable records remain untouched. Earlier parity/performance claims are not upgraded.
